messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: streaming-service.pulse p95=1.2s p99=3.6s (SLO breach) for 6m. Elevated tail latency and intermittent streaming stalls. Alerting oncall. dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/streams/pulse
ryan_oncall: ack — joining. any deployment or rollout in last 30m?
anya_sre: no deploys in last 45m. looking at recent traces and KV hit rates.
maya_infra: node-level metrics show GPU kernel busy spiking on pod group "streaming-worker-a" around t-7m. memory pressure low.
ellie_support: support queue: ~12 customer retries in last 10m, two customers reporting timeouts on long responses. attaching sample request ids: r-8a1f, r-8a2b
james_product: customer-impact: could be degraded UX for streaming integrations. prioritize quick mitigation and postmortem.
ryan_oncall: quick checklist: 1) confirm kvcache hit rate 2) check batching throttle 3) fallback model route 4) consider temporary autoscaler bump. who's on kv?
anya_sre: running quick query for prefix/KV hit rate... results: global kv_hit_rate dropped from 94% -> 67% coincident with spike. likely cold-prefix churn.
maya_infra: autoscaler shows no scale events. pods at 85% CPU, GPU util at 92% on a few nodes. not saturating network.
anya_sre: hypothesis: cache churn + larger batch sizes causing long tail (GPU kernel queueing). propose immediate mitigation: reduce batch_max_tokens and enable fallback variant that has smaller context.
ryan_oncall: execute mitigation steps, i'll coordinate:
- set batching throttle to 0.5 (quick throttle)
- route 20% traffic to fallback small-model variant
- warm prefix cache for top-10 prefixes if feasible

maya_infra: running command to set throttle: ```redwoodctl config set streaming-service.batch_throttle 0.5 --env prod```
maya_infra: throttle applied.
anya_sre: routing canary: ```redwoodctl route shift --service streaming-service --from main --to small-model-v2 --percent 20```
anya_sre: canary in flight, watching p95/p99.
ryan_oncall: warming top prefixes: starting background prefetch job for prefixes ["/chat/stream","/embed/precompute","/user/context/summary"] (low-impact).
ellie_support: support: informing affected customers of mitigation steps, will escalate if errors continue.
maya_infra: seeing immediate p99 drop from 3.6s -> 1.8s on canary traffic; global p99 trending down now.
anya_sre: KV hit rate improving to 82% after prefetch warms. still watching for secondary spikes.
james_product: good. prepare short note for customers if this persists >1h.
ryan_oncall: if latency holds, we'll keep fallback at 20% for 30m then roll down. if it flares, prepare oncall bridge.
anya_sre: logging quick repro steps and saving traces to `/incidents/3333334444/` for postmortem. (trace ids: t-7f2, t-7f3)
ellie_support: updating ticket #INC-4221 with mitigation and ETA.
maya_infra: autoscaler policy tweak proposal: add pod cushion 10% for streaming-worker-a to avoid kernel queueing during prefix churn. will PR after incident.
ryan_oncall: handoff — i'm staying until p99 < 1s sustained for 20m. if chat needed escalate to eng-oncall. thanks team. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Note: incident page created — https://incidents.redwood.ai/3333334444 (status: mitigation in progress)
summary: SLO breach for streaming-service.pulse (p99 spike). Mitigation: throttle batching, route 20% to smaller model variant, prefetch top prefixes. KV hit rate drop likely root cause; monitoring and follow-up tasks assigned.
